stories.headline: UK PM Burnham says Brexit failed and seeks a reset with the EU
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Britain has lost more than it gained from leaving the EU.
He called the 'hard Brexit' not good enough and compared it to 'The Emperor's New Clothes'.
A UK-EU summit takes place in Brussels on Friday.
stories.joke: The emperor has noticed the draught.
stories.vc: Closer EU ties could cut trade friction for UK exporters and lift the pound.

stories.headline: Yemen's army reports 661 attacks as Houthis push toward Aden
body: Yemen's army says it carried out 661 attacks on Houthi positions as the group advances toward Aden.
They included air strikes, artillery, drones and rockets.
Government forces have suffered a series of setbacks in the southwest.
stories.vc: Fighting near Bab al-Mandeb threatens one of the world's key shipping lanes.

stories.statLabel: collapse at the heart of the case
stories.headline: Paraguay's ex-president moved to military jail after special-treatment reports
body: A judge ordered former president Santiago Peña moved to a military prison.
Reports said he had a dining room, furniture and a private gym where he was being held.
He faces corruption charges linked to the collapse of Ueno Bank.
stories.vc: A big bank collapse shakes savers' trust in Paraguay's financial system.

image.credit: Bwood720 at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 512 points as foreign money flows in
body: The Sensex rose 512 points to 82,104.79 on Monday, and the Nifty closed at 25,291.
FMCG and bank shares led the gains; Max Healthcare was the top gainer.
Mid and small caps fell, with the Smallcap 100 down 1.1%.
stories.joke: Big caps party, small caps nap.
stories.vc: Foreign inflows and cheaper oil are keeping big Indian stocks in demand.

stories.headline: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24M for AI image sensors
body: Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in seed funding to build AI-enabled image sensors.
It says it has design wins with US defence firm General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon.
It aims to start commercial production in 2027.
stories.joke: Pre-revenue, but already seeing the future.
stories.vc: India wants to become a chip hub as firms look beyond China.

stories.headline: Karnataka halts new Green SM taxi registrations after union protests
body: Karnataka has stopped new registrations for Vietnam-based Green SM's electric taxis, days after clearing it.
Local taxi unions had protested its entry into Bengaluru.
The state also plans to make fare meters compulsory for all cabs, including Ola and Uber.
stories.joke: Meters are back. Surge pricing, take note.
stories.vc: Policy U-turns add risk for foreign mobility firms entering India.

stories.headline: Nvidia reports its first results without Jensen Huang
body: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, the first since Huang quit.
Questions include claims that its restricted chips were smuggled into China.
Nvidia has promised an internal investigation. (The FT's Unhedged had no new episode, so this is TechCrunch's preview.)
stories.vc: Nvidia's numbers and outlook steer the whole AI stock trade.

stories.headline: AI security startup Corma hits $1B valuation three months after launch
body: Corma raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation, led by NEA.
It sells AI models and agents trained to defend against cyberattacks.
Demand jumped after a wave of security flaws on October 21. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's deal.)
stories.joke: From stealth to unicorn faster than a password reset.
stories.vc: Investors are rushing into AI security as attacks speed up.

stories.headline: Ex-Freshworks team raises $53M to take on Salesforce
body: Dreamteam, founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million for an AI-native CRM.
Together Fund and Accel led the rounds, with Premji Invest joining.
Its AI pulls in context from emails and calls so salespeople don't type updates.
stories.joke: Finally, a CRM that does the data entry for you.
stories.vc: Indian-origin SaaS teams keep drawing big global rounds.

stories.headline: Stratechery: Huang's fall ends more than just a CEO's run
body: Ben Thompson argues Huang's exit marks the end of several things at once.
He says Nvidia came to be treated like a defence contractor, and Huang never adjusted.
He links it to Nvidia's long-term prospects and the AI boom.
stories.vc: If Nvidia is treated as a defence firm, its China sales and growth face lasting limits.

stories.headline: US moves to stop China renting AI chips abroad
body: The US is rolling out rules requiring licences to send AI chips to data centres anywhere that may serve Chinese firms.
It targets companies from the D:5 group, including China, Russia, Iran and North Korea.
The aim is to close the remote-access loophole. (No checkable Economist piece today, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Can't buy the chip? Can't rent it either.
stories.vc: Cloud firms in Asia and the Gulf face new paperwork and lost Chinese demand.

stories.headline: Serena Williams launches a new $200M venture fund
body: Serena Williams and partner Beth Ferreira have launched Starfire Ventures, aiming to raise $200 million.
It will back AI-native startups in areas like fintech and health.
Her earlier firm, Serena Ventures, backed over 100 companies and has made its last new investment.
stories.vc: Women-led funds remain rare, so a $200M fund is a big signal.

stories.statLabel: years the two men were jailed
stories.headline: Supreme Court grants bail to two convicts in Bilkis Bano case
body: The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two men convicted in the Bilkis Bano case and granted them bail.
They were convicted of her gang rape and the murder of her family in 2002.
The court cited over 17 years in jail and open issues in their appeal.
stories.vc: Survivors' trust in the justice system is the issue at stake.

stories.headline: Maharashtra orders C-section audits as private rates hit 59%
body: Maharashtra has ordered regular audits of caesarean deliveries.
About 59% of women delivering in private hospitals had C-sections, against 37% in public ones.
The goal is to make sure surgery happens only when medically needed.
stories.vc: Unneeded C-sections raise costs for families and insurers.

stories.headline: Karnataka to add 200 beds at Bengaluru's Kidwai cancer hospital
body: Karnataka will add 200 beds at the Kidwai Institute of Oncology in Bengaluru, DCM D.K. Shivakumar said.
It is also weighing 3 acres for housing families of children being treated.
Kidwai serves patients from across the state.
stories.joke: More beds, shorter waits. That's the plan.
stories.vc: More public cancer beds can cut long waits and costly private care.

stories.headline: Aster to open a 300-bed hospital in Hyderabad by March 2027
body: Aster DM Quality Care's 300-bed hospital at Kondapur, Hyderabad, will open in March 2027.
It costs ₹500 crore and takes Aster's Hyderabad beds past 1,700.
The group plans about ₹4,000 crore of investment over two years.
stories.joke: Hyderabad's skyline gets a few more stethoscopes.
stories.vc: Hospital chains are betting big on bed growth in fast-growing cities.

stories.headline: Tiruchy's Thuvakudi hospital seeks upgrade to an accident care centre
body: Thuvakudi Government Hospital near Tiruchy wants to become a TAEI accident and emergency centre.
That would bring more doctors and nurses and a CT scanner.
It sees 10 to 15 crash victims a day and sends about five to MGMGH.
stories.vc: Local trauma care saves lives and eases load on the city's big hospital.

stories.headline: NewEra Hospitals opens a newborn ICU in Vashi
body: NewEra Hospitals in Vashi has opened a dedicated neonatal intensive care unit.
It will care for premature, low-weight and sick newborns.
It has warmers, monitors, 24/7 breathing support and family-friendly spaces.
stories.vc: Specialist newborn units help private hospitals win more maternity patients.

stories.headline: India's Graviton now earns more in Singapore than at home
body: Graviton Research Capital's Singapore arm nearly tripled its profit to $142.4 million in the year to March 2026.
Its Indian unit earned 25% less, about $94 million.
The jump makes co-founders Nishil and Ankit Gupta worth about $1 billion each, Bloomberg reports.
stories.joke: Two IIT Delhi friends, one very fast billion.
stories.vc: Indian HFT firms are growing faster abroad than at home.

stories.headline: Thailand's stock exchange tightens oversight of high-frequency trading
body: The Stock Exchange of Thailand announced eight revised trading measures.
They include smaller tick sizes, new short-selling rules and closer watch on high-frequency trading.
The aim is cheaper, more efficient trading and more investor confidence.
stories.vc: Smaller ticks can mean tighter prices for investors but thinner margins for market makers.

stories.statLabel: of the profit went to algo firms
stories.headline: Explainer: what is HFT, and why do algos win in India?
body: High-frequency trading (HFT) means computers buying and selling in tiny fractions of a second.
Many HFT firms are market makers: they offer to buy a bit lower and sell a bit higher, and keep the small gap, called the spread.
SEBI data show algo firms took 99% of the trading profit made by prop traders and foreign investors last year.
stories.joke: Your thumb versus a server: not a fair race.
stories.vc: Speed and tech spending, not hunches, decide who wins in HFT.

stories.headline: Haas keeps rookie Câmara in the car for Las Vegas
body: Rafael Câmara will race for Haas again at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Ryo Hirakawa takes Ollie Bearman's car in first practice.
Haas dropped Esteban Ocon during the Mexico City weekend; Câmara joins full-time next year.
stories.joke: Vegas rule: stick with what's working.
stories.vc: Young drivers on cheaper deals help midfield teams manage budgets.
